paper_metadata.title: Quantum Computation for Pricing Caps using the LIBOR Market Model

summary: The paper presents two simulation-based gate-model approaches for cap pricing under the LIBOR Market Model: a hybrid Monte Carlo + iterative QAE method using 3 qubits for distribution loading, and a pure quantum QAE method using 18 qubits for a 3-year cap example. Both are benchmarked against Black-76 and classical Monte Carlo; the paper reports better convergence for the hybrid method and lower low-sample error for the pure quantum method, but no hardware demonstration or practical quantum advantage.

experiments.description: Hybrid classical-quantum cap pricing under the LIBOR Market Model using Monte Carlo for earlier tenors and iterative quantum amplitude estimation for the last alive tenor.

algorithm.variant: hybrid classical-quantum iterative quantum amplitude estimation (IQAE) for cap pricing

problem_formulation.encoding_details: A discretized log-normal distribution for the final forward rate is loaded into a 3-qubit register; the payoff is encoded via Ry rotations and estimated with QAE. Earlier tenors are simulated classically by Monte Carlo.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the expected payoff of the last caplet under the LIBOR Market Model and sum with classically simulated earlier caplets to price the cap.

problem_instance.description: Pricing interest rate caps under the LIBOR Market Model using benchmark forward rates and implied volatilities from Brigo and Mercurio (2006).
problem_instance.dataset_name: Brigo and Mercurio (2006) benchmark LIBOR forward rates and implied volatilities

dataset_specification.description: Observed LIBOR rate at t=0 is 4.69%; forward rates and piecewise-constant implied volatilities are taken from the benchmark setup in the paper.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Forward rates are simulated under the LMM with log-normal dynamics; the final tenor distribution is discretized into a 3-qubit probability distribution for QAE.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Pricing results compared against Black-76 theoretical value; 50 trials for average absolute error in Fig. 3(b); 100 replicated experiments for qubit-number sweep in Fig. 4(a).

implementation_details.classical_solver: Monte Carlo simulation on classical computer; Black-76 formula used as theoretical benchmark
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical Monte Carlo simulates forward rates until the second-last alive tenor; discretized log-normal distribution loaded into quantum register.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Caplet prices are summed classically to obtain cap price.

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: Convergence/error decreases with more Monte Carlo samples; hybrid method outperforms classical Monte Carlo in estimation error.

results.uncertainty: Figure 3(b) reports average absolute deviation over 50 trials, but no numeric error values are stated in the text provided.
95% CI not numerically specified in the provided text

speedup_claims.conditions: QAE error scaling compared with Monte Carlo error scaling
speedup_claims.caveats: Claim is about asymptotic estimation error scaling (O(1/M) vs O(1/sqrt(M))); not a wall-clock runtime benchmark.

speedup_claims.conditions: for the tested cap pricing instances and sample counts
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the hybrid method consistently has lower estimation error and converges faster, but does not provide a single numeric speedup factor.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Quadratic improvement in estimation error scaling via QAE (error O(1/M) vs classical Monte Carlo O(1/sqrt(M)))

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 3 qubits for the hybrid distribution-loading example; iterative QAE used, but no hardware execution or resource benchmark is reported
limiting_factors: Only simulated cap pricing is shown
Classical Monte Carlo baseline remains the comparator
No circuit depth or gate counts reported

experiments.description: Pure quantum cap pricing under the LIBOR Market Model using QAE to estimate the expected payoff of every caplet and sum them quantumly/classically.

algorithm.variant: pure quantum iterative quantum amplitude estimation (IQAE) for all caplets

hyperparameters.number_of_states_example: 8 states at t=1 implies 64 states at t=2 for same accuracy

problem_formulation.encoding_details: A multivariate log-normal distribution for multiple caplets is loaded into separate quantum registers; comparator circuits mark payoffs above strike; Ry gates encode payoff amplitudes.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the expected payoff of each caplet under the LIBOR Market Model and aggregate to obtain the cap price.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Comparator circuits C[id < K] set the indicator qubit when caplet value exceeds strike.

problem_instance.description: Pricing a 3-year cap under the LIBOR Market Model using benchmark forward rates and implied volatilities from Brigo and Mercurio (2006).
problem_instance.dataset_name: Brigo and Mercurio (2006) benchmark LIBOR forward rates and implied volatilities

dataset_specification.description: Observed LIBOR rate at t=0 is 4.69%; forward rates and piecewise-constant implied volatilities are taken from the benchmark setup in the paper.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Each caplet’s probability distribution is discretized according to maturity; the full cap uses 18 qubits to load the multivariate distribution in the example.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Pricing results compared against Black-76 theoretical value; sample mean and 95% confidence interval over 50 replicated experiments in Fig. 4(a).

implementation_details.classical_solver: Black-76 formula used as theoretical benchmark; classical Monte Carlo used for comparison in figures
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical simulation and discretization of the underlying forward-rate distributions; 3i-qubit loading per caplet maturity.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Caplet prices are summed to obtain the cap price.

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: Pure quantum method is more accurate at low sample counts but becomes harder to improve due to large circuit depth and qubit count.

results.uncertainty: Figure 4(a) reports mean and 95% confidence intervals over 50 replicated experiments, but the provided text does not give the full numeric error bars for each qubit setting.
95% CI not numerically specified in the provided text

speedup_claims.caveats: The pure quantum method is reported to be more accurate at low simulation counts, but becomes difficult to improve due to circuit depth and qubit requirements.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Quadratic improvement in estimation error scaling via QAE (error O(1/M) vs classical Monte Carlo O(1/sqrt(M)))
